text: Edward William McBride (ca 1791 – September 3, 1834) was a businessman and political figure in Upper Canada. Born in Newark (Niagara-on-the-Lake) around 1791, he was the son of a United Empire Loyalist. He served in the local militia during the War of 1812. He worked as assistant to King's Printer John Cameron and assumed the role when Cameron became ill in April 1815, continuing until February 1816, several months after Cameron's death. After that, he operated an inn at Niagara. In 1824, he was elected to the Legislative Assembly of Upper Canada for the town of Niagara as a Reformer. He supported government funding for the Welland Canal and defended those who supported Robert Gourlay. For a time, he co-published the Niagara Herald, a newspaper owned by John Crooks, alongside Bartemas Ferguson. As a freemason, he was accused of being associated with the kidnapping and presumed murder of Captain William Morgan, who is said to have revealed secrets of the order. Although McBride denied these accusations, this contributed to his defeat in the 1828 election. He died in Niagara in 1834.
